From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## 1. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim

The preamble says the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are not to be re-opened. I can't verify that, and nothing in our record supports it.

- Two of the Seller's numbers, the **20% / AUD 4.8m cap** and the **18-month period**, are exactly our conditional fallbacks. Each needs **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft**, and none has been given.
- The other terms (AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k deductible basket, title under the general regime, buyer-knowledge exclusion, post-completion Riverlark release) are not within any fallback we hold.
- The "market standard" statements are the Seller's assertions and no evidence is attached. They shouldn't drive our response.

**Action:** Do not treat anything as agreed. Please confirm with Amelia whether she has agreed anything with the Seller's principal. If she has, we need it in writing and tied to this draft. Our mark-up should go back at playbook positions and be silent on "FINAL".

## 2. Departures from the playbook

### A. Liability regime

| Item | Seller | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start | Seller is at our *fallback*, which is not authorised. Counter at AUD 6m. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, **deductible** (excess only) | AUD 50,000, **tipping** (first dollar) | 5x higher and the wrong mechanism. |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months | Again our unauthorised fallback. |

The thresholds compound. A claim under AUD 25k is excluded outright, so it can't count toward the basket. Even claims that qualify lose the first AUD 250k. Combined with a AUD 4.8m cap, a large share of realistic warranty losses would be unrecoverable. Seller describes the AUD 250k basket as "around 1% of price", but 1% of AUD 24m is AUD 240k, which is roughly 5x our figure.

### B. Title and fundamental warranties (cl. 12.3/13 and "Fundamental/Title")

The Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity". Cl. 12.3/13 also says any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".

This is a **hidden general-regime override**. Together they would drag Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and fraud into the general cap, basket and 18-month limit. It directly contradicts our playbook:
- Fundamental/Title claims need a separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years.
- They must sit outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories must stay separate.

**Push back:** Reverse the default. General limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims, and every other category is expressly carved out.

### C. Fraud carve-out missing (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature". That expressly captures fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Our playbook says these must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and that **no one may waive this**. This is non-negotiable. It also shouldn't be traded for movement elsewhere.

### D. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2)

The Seller discloses the entire indexed data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records. This is the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure we reject. We require **specific fair disclosure** against identified warranties.

- The specific items in sections 2–10 of the letter are useful factual statements, and we should keep them as the basis for specific disclosure.
- Cl. 1.4 (no admission of breach, materiality, loss or legal requirement) is unobjectionable as a Seller statement of position. It must not operate to limit warranties or indemnities or to characterise the disclosed matters.
- Cl. 11 ("Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record") reads like a knowledge or reliance hook. Strike it or neutralise it.
- Disclosure must not qualify title and capacity warranties, specific indemnities or fraud claims.

### E. Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)

The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". Combined with the general disclosure, this is a double exclusion and a constructive-knowledge trap. **Delete it.** If a knowledge qualifier is ever conceded, it must use named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry. It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### F. Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)

Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%). The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".

- **The documents are inconsistent.** The update says the matter is "addressed", but Disclosure Letter §2 admits there is no final written consent and no evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Playbook: require **effective consent and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**. Consent-on-delivery is not enough, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.

**Push back:** Make it a condition precedent, waivable only by the Buyer. Require the consent in agreed form, with evidence that the cl. 11.3 conditions are met and no adverse conditions attached.

### G. Riverlark (cl. 2 / 7)

About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion". Letter §3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.

Playbook requires:
- a current payout figure
- direct repayment to Riverlark from Completion funds
- effective security releases

A post-completion release is acceptable only with an **irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval**, and neither exists. The AUD 3.2m is also Debt on a debt-free/cash-free basis, so it must be dealt with in the price mechanics.

### H. Employee bonuses (DD-005)

AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses are left out of the funds flow as "a matter for the Seller". Letter §5 confirms they don't appear in the flow and doesn't say whether payroll tax, super or other on-costs apply.

**Push back:** Either a specific funds-flow line item (bonuses plus triggered on-costs, deducted from price or paid from Seller proceeds) or an express Seller-funded obligation. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position and how it was calculated. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

### I. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1)

The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and the Seller calls it adequate. DD-004 cl. 7.3 conditions the transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee, so the exposure is about IP ownership, not only a payment.

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to losses and claims arising from the Ironquay matter, including IP ownership, use and third-party claims.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment, then confirmatory assignment.
- Keep it as a specific indemnity outside the general limits.
- Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified in both directions. DD-010 says it is not bank verification, and no receipt or assignment is in the data room. Ask for bank evidence either way.

### J. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Sch 6)

The Seller says it is "preliminary… not expected to be material". Its own letter says the investigation is preliminary and that access, scope and any notification duty are unknown. The Seller therefore has no basis for a materiality conclusion, and we shouldn't accept it.

In the other direction, we shouldn't assume a breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar figure. Seek procedural protection:
- log preservation
- completion of the investigation
- regular written updates and access to findings
- consultation before any notification decision
- cooperation covenants

Whether to seek a specific indemnity, without any numeric demand, is a call for the deal team.

### K. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000: 3 × AUD 110,000)

The Seller calls them ordinary-course operating costs. Letter §8 doesn't say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We shouldn't accept the Seller's label, and we shouldn't assume the opposite. Request the contracts (DD-008, DD-011) and assess terms, timing and accrual. **No automatic Debt classification or price deduction either way.**

### L. Tax / IP

The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime". They are **open** on our side. Reject the statement and keep them as separate categories with no override from the general regime. Don't assume unlimited liability or any resolution.

### M. Title

Title rests on the DD-012 share register, which is a supplied internal Seller source and not independent proof. Letter §10 itself says the Buyer hasn't completed verification. Require independent evidence of:
- ownership and the chain of title
- encumbrances (including whether any Riverlark security touches the shares)
- Seller authority and capacity

Suggested sources: an ASIC extract, a certified register copy, issue and transfer documents, board and shareholder approvals, and security-interest searches. These are for the diligence team to settle.

### N. Items to check, not conclude

For the lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009), the letter says the material doesn't *describe* consent as required for a share sale. That is not confirmation that no consent is needed. Have the team read the actual clauses (including any change-of-control wording) before we rely on it.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Do not concede (non-negotiable):**
1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
2. A separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge.
3. Deletion of the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (cl. 8.3).
4. Specific fair disclosure only. Strike the whole-data-room, public-register and Accounts deemed disclosure.
5. Reversal of the "applies to all Claims" default in cl. 12.3/13, 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5.

**Counter at playbook positions:**
6. Cap AUD 6m (25%), de minimis AUD 5k, tipping basket AUD 50k, 24 months.
7. Bluefen: condition precedent requiring effective consent plus evidence its conditions are satisfied.
8. Riverlark: payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion.
9. Bonuses: a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, including on-costs.
10. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and seek bank and assignment evidence.
11. DD-006: preservation, investigation, updates and cooperation, with no assumptions about breach or amounts.
12. Title: independent evidence beyond DD-012.
13. Tax and IP stay open and separate.
14. Sandbar: assess the contracts, with no automatic Debt treatment.

**Escalate to Amelia Frost before responding:**
- Whether any principal-level understanding exists. If so, get it in writing and tied to this draft.
- Whether she wants to authorise either fallback (20% cap, 18 months). Neither is authorised now, and any authority must identify the draft.
- Whether a post-completion Riverlark release could ever be acceptable. It would need an irrevocable undertaking and her approval.

**Suggested tactics:** Because the Seller's own letter admits that Bluefen consent, the Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment evidence and the bonus funds flow are all unresolved, we can state that "FINAL" cannot apply to a package with open conditions. Cite the Seller's disclosures back at them to support the mark-up.

I can turn this into a mark-up issues list or a draft response letter to Seller's counsel if that would help.
